Before processing the card request, I performed a quick relationship review, noting the recent contacts on the acct.
I mentioned to her, "Looks like we've been in touch a couple of times recently, I just want to make sure all your other concerns have been taken care of."
Cx acknowledged this. She brought up the fraud dispute from back in March. Mentioned the "weird charge from that luggage place" and said what a headache it was. She confirmed that she did see the provisional credit post to her acct, which she was very happy about. Seems satisfied with how that was handled.
I also saw the recent email correspondence note. I asked if she had received the paper statement she requested last month.

[2026-05-20 - 17:15 UTC | BRANCH_SUPPORT] C05 BRANCH VISIT WRITE-UP (part 1/3)
Cx Sofia Doyle in branch approx. 2:15 PM. Was a walk-in. Seemed a bit stressed but was very polite.
Primary issue is w/ her physical card.

- Cx presented her Chase Slate Edge card (*2837) for inspection.
- Card is in very poor shape. The top right corner is completely snapped off, and the magnetic stripe is visibly scratched and worn down. Cx says she's had it for a long time.
- Per cx, she has been having intermittent issues with it for weeks, where she has to swipe it multiple times at a terminal.
- Today, the swipe function failed entirely at a local business. She said the chip still works, so she was able to complete that purchase, but she is concerned the whole card will just stop working soon. She is traveling from her home in Charlotte and doesn't want to be left without a usable card.

Pulled up cx acct to begin.
Verified cx identity using her NC driver's license. Photo and info match what we have on file. Completed CCK verification questions, all answers correct.
Noted the address in Charlotte and asked about her visit. She's here for another week visiting her sister.
Before processing the card request, I performed a quick relationship review, noting the recent contacts on the acct.
I mentioned to her, "Looks like we've been in touch a couple of times recently, I just want to make sure all your other concerns have been taken care of."
Cx acknowledged this. She brought up the fraud dispute from back in March. Mentioned the "weird charge from that luggage place" and said what a headache it was. She confirmed that she did see the provisional credit post to her acct, which she was very happy about. Seems satisfied with how that was handled.
I also saw the recent email correspondence note. I asked if she had received the paper statement she requested last month.

snapshot.fact:
[2026-05-20 - 17:15 UTC | BRANCH_SUPPORT] C05 BRANCH VISIT WRITE-UP (part 2/3)
She confirmed she did receive it. Stated, "Oh yes, thank you. My wife, Renata, and I find it much easier to have the physical copies for our records. We're a bit old-fashioned that way." This aligns with notes from a prior call.
I also wanted to proactively confirm her contact info. I saw the note about the email change. I read the email on file, sofia.doyle73@example.net, back to her to ensure it was correct.
Cx confirmed it. "Yes, that's it. I'm so glad that agent I chatted with double-checked. I'm terrible at typing and almost gave them the wrong one."
Finally, I confirmed the callback number on file (608-555-0481). She said yes, that's her office landline and it's the most reliable way to reach her if needed, as her cell service can be spotty.

Moved on to resolving the card issue.
Advised cx that given the physical damage, the best course of action is to order a replacement.
I explained the options. We can order a new card via standard mail, or we can expedite it for a fee.
Cx asked how long standard mail would take. Advised approx. 5-7 business days.
She declined the expedited shipping, stating that since the chip on her current card (*2837) still works, she is okay to wait for the standard delivery to her home address.
She asked a key question: will ordering a new card deactivate her current one?
I assured her that the current card, *2837, will remain fully active and usable until she receives the new replacement card in the mail and calls to activate it. This seemed to be her main concern.
I proceeded with the replacement card order in the system.
Selected reason code for DAMAGED/WORN card.
Confirmed her mailing address in Charlotte is correct for the delivery.
Submitted the order. I've pasted the system confirmation note below for the record.
---

ACCT: ...-XXXX
CARD REPLACEMENT ORDER SUBMITTED 20-MAY-2026 14:28 EST

[2026-08-31 - 14:45 UTC | BRANCH_SUPPORT] C11 BRANCH VISIT WRITE-UP (part 1/3)
Customer Sofia Doyle (resides in Charlotte, NC) came into the branch today around 2:30 PM. Seemed a little stressed but was very pleasant. I pulled up her profile after completing standard KYC verification with her driver's license. She said she had a few different things to discuss.

Her first question was about getting a cashier's check. She's moving to a new apartment locally and needs it for the security deposit and first month's rent. We talked for a minute about the Charlotte rental market, she said it's been a real challenge finding a place and she's just glad it's over. I confirmed she had sufficient funds in her checking account to cover the check.

As I was getting ready to process the request, she held up her hand and said, "Actually, can we pause on that for one second? I have another question that's been on my mind." She then brought up a recent dispute she had filed. She couldn't remember the exact details but mentioned it was about some luggage that was never delivered. I saw the closed case in her history and was able to confirm it was resolved in her favor. She was very happy about that, said "Oh good, I just wanted to make sure that was permanent. That $473.31 was a lot to lose, and you guys handled it really well, so thank you." I told her she was welcome and that we were glad it worked out.

This seemed to lead into her next train of thought, which was more forward-looking. She got a little quiet and then asked about the process for closing an account. She was very quick to clarify, saying, and I am quoting this directly because she was very emphatic: "I am NOT closing the account, I just want to know what the steps would be." She explained that with her move, she's been trying to "get her financial house in order" and was just curious what the process looked like, in case she ever decided to consolidate her banking relationships in the future.

snapshot.fact:
[2026-08-31 - 14:45 UTC | BRANCH_SUPPORT] C11 BRANCH VISIT WRITE-UP (part 2/3)
I explained that it's a straightforward process. We'd need to ensure the account has a zero balance, with no pending transactions or automatic payments scheduled. Any direct deposits would need to be rerouted first. Once clear, she could close it either in a branch or by sending a written request. I took this as an opportunity for a soft retention effort. I mentioned that we value her as a customer and would be sorry to see her go, even hypothetically. I also told her about a targeted promotion we have running right now for a $200.00 statement credit on her Chase Slate Edge card if she hits a certain spend threshold over the next quarter. She seemed interested but didn't commit, just said "Oh, that's good to know, thank you."

Then she pivoted back to her original request. "Okay, thank you for explaining all that. Very helpful. Now, about that cashier's check..." I re-confirmed the payee name (the property management company) and the total amount. She needed the check before the end of the day as the lease signing is tomorrow morning. She mentioned that the landlord needs the security deposit cleared by the end of next month, but she wanted to get it all done at once. I processed the check request, printed it, and had my manager provide the second signature. While we waited, I double-checked her contact information on file to make sure it was current after her move. I confirmed her email is doyle.s99@example.org and her best callback number is 608-555-0779, which she said was correct. She mentioned the number was new-ish, her work line, and was glad we had it right.

Cx Ingrid Okafor came into the branch today, approx 11:15am. Seemed a little frustrated but was very pleasant.
Pulled her profile after standard CCK. ID verified.
Primary reason for visit: her Amazon Prime Visa card (*6824).

Cx states that for the past week or so, the chip on the card has been failing.
- It’s not being read at terminals.
- First time it happened was at the grocery store, had to swipe, held up the line, very embarrassing per cx.
- Has happened multiple times since. Sometimes the swipe works, sometimes it doesn't.
- She tried cleaning the chip w/ an alcohol wipe, her brother Emeka told her to try that, didn't help.
- Worried she’s going to get stuck somewhere unable to pay.
- Asked if this is a common problem. I told her it happens sometimes, cards get demagnetized or the chip just wears out over time.

Took a look at the card itself. No visible damage, no cracks or obvious scratches on the chip, but it does look a little worn. Looks like a classic chip failure.

While I was looking at her account, I noticed the recent case activity. Asked her if everything was sorted with that one charge she’d been looking into a while back.
- She lit up a bit, said "Oh, the ski rental thing? Yes, thank goodness."
- Said the provisional credit showed up, which she was happy about.
- Mentioned how weird it was, b/c she lives in San Diego and hasn't seen snow in years, let alone rented skis. Said it must have been some kind of data breach. I agreed it was likely.
- Cx mentioned that incident is what made her want to get paper statements again, just to have a hard copy to go over. She remembered getting an email about it and said she appreciated the quick response. Confirmed she received the itemized copy she'd requested. She said not yet, but she knows it can take a little time in the mail.

Customer Andre Haddad came into the branch today around 2:30 PM. He's a local, lives over in Atlanta, GA, and was pleasant to work with. He had his Chase Slate Edge card (*7093) ready for identification. I greeted him and brought him back to my desk. Standard verification procedures followed.

ID SCAN COMPLETE - GA DL / CUST VERIFIED VIA PIN PAD

Mr. Haddad said he needed to get a cashier's check. He's working on a project, he said, and needed to pay a specialist vendor. When I asked for the amount and the payee name, he got a little flustered. He had the amount ready but had to check his phone for the exact spelling of the business name. He laughed and said his memory wasn't what it used to be. While he was looking, I made some small talk. I noticed the notes on his file and mentioned I was glad to see that issue with the florist had been resolved in his favor. He nodded and said, "Oh, yeah, the $602.64 thing. What a headache that was." He seemed genuinely relieved it was over and appreciative that I'd noticed. He said dealing with dispute DSP-2174159 had been a pain but the resolution was handled well once it got going.

He found the payee name on his phone ("Vintage Steel Restorations LLC") and I began the process of drawing up the check from his primary checking. As the system was loading, he suddenly switched topics completely.

He leaned forward a bit and lowered his voice, "You know, while I'm here, I have a kind of general question. Not something I'm doing today, or even soon, but I was just thinking about it. What's the process if someone wants to close their accounts?" He immediately put his hands up, very insistent, and said, "I am NOT closing the account, I just want to know what the steps would be. I've been with you guys for years, I'm just curious about the procedure."

snapshot.name: projects/410688210853/locations/us-central1/reasoningEngines/7552091822646886400/memories/533517332815806464
snapshot.fact:
[2026-08-31 - 16:40 UTC | BRANCH_SUPPORT] C11 BRANCH VISIT WRITE-UP (part 2/3)
I assured him it was a perfectly normal question and that I was happy to walk him through the hypothetical steps. I explained that he could do it in a branch, over the phone, or by written request. We'd need to make sure all his balances were zero and that there were no pending transactions. I mentioned that for his credit card, any remaining rewards points would be forfeited upon closure, so it's always best to redeem them beforehand. I also mentioned that closing a long-held credit card can sometimes have a small impact on a person's credit score due to the change in average age of accounts and credit utilization, so it's something to be aware of.

He seemed to be listening intently. He asked a few follow-up questions about whether it was instant or took a few days. I explained that once initiated, it's pretty quick, but we always advise waiting a few business days after the last transaction clears just to be safe. Since he seemed concerned about the "value" of the account, I took the opportunity to softly pivot to retention. I told him we value his business and that there are often promotions available to long-time customers. I mentioned, just as an example, that we sometimes run targeted offers like a $200.00 statement credit for meeting a certain spend threshold over a few months, and that it's always worth calling the number on the back of his card to see if any offers are available to him. He just nodded and said "good to know," but didn't seem interested in pursuing it, which was fine. His focus was clearly on the "what if" scenario.
